summary: The last 4 weeks show a fragmented, low-volume training block with very poor recovery — sleep has repeatedly fallen below 5 hours, body battery has hit critically low values (2 on July 30th, 5 on July 27th), and the only high-intensity run (July 18th, avg HR 179 bpm) was a significant spike with no apparent build rationale. Cycling has been the most consistent discipline with one strong 77km ride, but swimming volume is minimal and running continuity is absent. With a sprint triathlon test race just 7 days away, the immediate priority must be arriving fresh rather than accumulating more fitness load.
suggestions: For the sprint test race in 7 days, treat this entire week as a taper: eliminate all high-intensity and long-duration sessions, keep any movement short (under 40 min), easy, and race-discipline specific — a short 750m open-water swim, a 20–25 min easy spin, and a 15-min easy run at race pace (around 5:30–5:45/km) are all you need.

Sleep is the single biggest limiter right now — you've had at least 6 nights under 5 hours in the last 4 weeks, which directly impairs recovery and raises injury risk; make 7+ hours a non-negotiable target every night this week before the race.

Your open-water swim pace (24–28 min/km) is far slower than the race target for the 750m leg — after the test race, dedicate at least two pool sessions per week to technique drills (catch, high-elbow pull) to close the gap toward the ≤2:30/100m target needed for Ironman Cervia.

The July 18th run at avg HR 179 bpm with 401W power is a red flag for uncontrolled intensity — future interval sessions must use strict HR caps (≤170 bpm) or power-based targets with a warm-up check, especially while sleep quality remains compromised.

After the test race, re-establish a consistent 3-discipline weekly structure (swim/bike/run) before adding volume; with Treviso 10K 64 days away, the priority from Week 9 onward should shift to run-specific work (tempo and intervals) while maintaining cycling aerobic base at Z2.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk6 Pool Swim (Friday) — 54 min, 2km+, ≤2:30/100m (AI adjusted to 30–40 min easy technique, 1,000–1,200m)
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 15–20 min easy pool or open-water swim, drills only (catch-up, fingertip drag), no pace target, max 600–800m — pure race familiarity, not a training stimulus.
proposed_changes.reason: Body battery was 2 on July 30th and the race is 7 days away — any meaningful training load today delays recovery without adding fitness.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk6 Long Ride (AI adjusted) — up to 150 min, 50–60km @ 128–145W
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Replace with a 35–40 min easy race-prep spin @ 120–140W (well below Z2 ceiling), flat route; include 3x30-second pickups at race effort (~160–170W) to wake up the legs — total duration strictly 40 min maximum.
proposed_changes.reason: A long ride 6 days before the test race will deepen fatigue, not build fitness; a short activation spin with brief race-effort touches is more appropriate.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk6 Long Run (AI adjusted) — 7–8km @ 7:00/km, HR ≤145 bpm, or 30-min walk if HR spikes
proposed_changes.proposed_session: 20–25 min easy run @ 6:30–7:00/km with 4x30-second strides at 5:30/km (race pace) near the end — total distance ~3–4km; stop immediately if HR exceeds 150 bpm during strides.
proposed_changes.reason: Five days before the race, a long run is counterproductive; a short run with race-pace strides primes the neuromuscular system without adding fatigue debt.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk7 Evening session (AI adjusted) — 60 min Z2 @ 128–155W (if body battery ≥40, else 40 min easy)
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Full rest or 20 min very easy spin @ 110–125W only — this is 3 days before race day and the body needs to be absorbing, not loading.
proposed_changes.reason: Three days pre-race, even a 60-min Z2 ride risks leaving residual fatigue in the legs for the bike leg on race day.

proposed_changes.proposed_session: 20–25 min pool swim: 400m easy warm-up, 4x50m at race effort with 20-sec rest, 200m easy cool-down — total ~1,000m, focus on feel and confidence not volume.
proposed_changes.reason: Three days before the race the 750m swim leg needs a confidence touch, not a 2km training stimulus that adds fatigue.

proposed_changes.current_session: Wk7 Evening session (AI adjusted) — 30 min easy run @ 6:45–7:00/km, HR ≤145 bpm
proposed_changes.proposed_session: Skip the run entirely — full rest or 15 min easy walk only; this is the day before race day and legs must be fresh for the 5km run leg.
proposed_changes.reason: Running the day before a triathlon race, even easy, adds unnecessary neuromuscular fatigue and risks arriving at the start line with heavy legs.
